synopsis: Chapter 12 identifies ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2:2022 as the standard for assurance cases [f9707]. The glossary specifies that it standardizes what an assurance case must contain and describes the case as a structured argument linking claims to evidence [f12254, f15353]. The booklet groups the standard with UL 4600 and Goal Structuring Notation as structured ways to organize a safety argument [f15380]. These facts are consistent, but do not enumerate the required contents or explain how the three approaches differ [f9707, f12254, f15353, f15380].

relations.note: Clarifies that standardization covers the required contents of an assurance case.
Describes the standardized assurance case as a structured argument linking claims to evidence.
Places the assurance-case standard alongside other structured safety-argument approaches.
Its claims-to-evidence structure explains its grouping among structured safety-argument approaches.
